subject: (Logistic growth) ODE model in Stan getting stuck before sampling begins

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: (Logistic growth) ODE model in Stan getting stuck before sampling begins
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to solve the following ODE in Stan (I know that analytic solutions exist for this ODE, but it's a stepping stone for more complex models I want to fit):

 real[] logistic_diff(real t,real[] y,real[] theta,real[] x_r,int[] x_i) {
    real dydt[1];
    
    dydt[1] <- theta[1] * y[1] * (1 - theta[2] * y[1]);

    return dydt;
    }

The above defines a logistic growth model. So it has a couple of parameters, and is only a system of a single variable. I assume a normal sampling model, with another parameter: sigma.

I can generate data for this model (attached) and have been trying to get Stan to fit the three parameters of the model (theta[1],theta[2],sigma), where the true values are (0.5,0.05,2). 

I am having an issue whereby Stan appears to get 'stuck' before it has begun to sample - it's really strange; it doesn't appear to be due to poor convergence, as it hasn't even outputted ``iteration 1/2000'' for example. It doesn't happen for every run, but only for about 1/4 where it seems to break my rstudio, and I am forced to kill the process manually.

I don't think this is due to slow convergence - I have 100 simulated datasets, and I know that in general this simple system is well-identified. 

Does anyone know what is going on? (The full model is below.)

Best,

Ben


functions {
    real[] logistic_diff(real t,real[] y,real[] theta,real[] x_r,int[] x_i) {
    real dydt[1];
    
    dydt[1] <- theta[1] * y[1] * (1 - theta[2] * y[1]);

    return dydt;
    }
}
data {
    int<lower=1> T;
    int<lower=0> N;
    real t0;
    real ts[T];
    matrix[T,N] y;
}
transformed data {
    real x_r[0];
    int x_i[0];
}

parameters {
      real<lower=0> theta[2];
      real<lower=0> sigma;
      real<lower=0> y0[1];
}


model {
  real y_hat[T,1];
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,1);
  theta ~ normal(0,2);
  y0 ~ normal(5,2);
  y_hat <- integrate_ode(logistic_diff, y0, t0, ts, theta, x_r, x_i);
  for (i in 1:N){
    for (t in 1:T) {
          y[t,i] ~ normal(y_hat[t,1],sigma);
      }
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] (Logistic growth) ODE model in Stan getting stuck before sampling begins
parts:
Ben, I was able to recover the parameters fine with RStan v2.9.0. I'm guessing there's something going on with how you generated data. Can you post your script? I'll try to replicate and figure out what's going on.

Here's mine:

theta <- c(0.5, 0.05)
sigma <- 2
y0 <- 5

N <- 10
T <- 20

library(deSolve)
t0 <- 0.0
ts <- 1:T

logistic_diff <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    dy <- theta_1 * y * (1 - theta_2 * y)
    list(c(dy))
  })
}
parameters <- c(theta_1 = theta[1], theta_2 = theta[2])
out <- ode(y = c(y = y0), times = c(t0, ts), func = logistic_diff, parms = parameters)

out <- out[-1, 2]

y <- matrix(out, T, N)
y <- y + matrix(rnorm(T * N, 0, sigma), T, N)

data <- list(T = T, N = N, t0 = t0, ts = ts, y = y)

library(rstan)
fit <- stan("ode_example.stan", data = data)
On Sun, Jun 19, 2016 at 9:46 AM, 'Ben Lambert' via Stan users mailing list <stan-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Great - I have put upper limits on my parameters for now, and that seems to solve the problem. (I will remove these when the new release comes out.) Thanks very much! Best, Ben

Wold you mind sharing the model and data? Ideally
the simplest model and data that have the problem.

The new ODE solvers shouldn't go into infinite loops,
so if they do, it's a bug. It could be the sampler
taking many leapfrog steps for a slow solver.

You can put refresh=1 on the output to track every
iteration and see if it's really iteration 1 where things
are getting stuck.

The other culprit can be very small step sizes.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: hanging ODE solver with 2.11
parts:
> On Aug 22, 2016, at 10:26 AM, Bram Thijssen <brams...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hey Bob & Sebastian,
>
> Did you have a chance to look at this?
>
> I've noticed now that if I put limits on the parameters with the pointy bracket notation (e.g. real<lower=0.0015, upper=0.15> theta1 in the parameters block), instead of with a prior (e.g. theta1 ~ uniform(0.0015, 0.15) in the model block), then it does work normally.

If you have theta1 ~ uniform(0.0015, 0.15) in the model block
then you are required to have the lower- and upper-bound
constraints real<lower=0.0015, upper=0.15>. The log density should
remain finite for any value of the parameters meeting the constraint.

So what's probably happening is that you're managing to initialize,
but then can't move because of rejections from parameter going
outside of (0.0015, 0.15).
> The sampler still has a lot of difficulty converging, but at least it's starting the sampling then. Does this give any clue what might be going on?

Yes :-)

Is there a natural constraint on theta1, such as theta1 in (0, 1)
or theta1 in (0, infinity)? If so, you may want to try a stronger
unconstrained prior, like normal(0.075, 0.07).

Another thing that will really help is if you can keep the parameters
on the unit scale---then Stan doesn't have to find the right scale
during warmup. So that'd be something like

theta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

theta = 0.07 * theta_raw + 0.075;

It's an ugly hack, but it can be hard for Stan to adapt for complex
models during warmup.

- Bob
